title: Controlplane tidy briefing — weekly pulse (2026-10-07)
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marcus, Priya, Evan, Sofia, + SRE drop-in (Leila).

Meeting objective: short weekly pulse to capture emergent routing/auth/quotas items, sync on canary health, and list next-step owners. Keep this as the canonical lightweight log for this week — not a full postmortem.

Agenda:
- Quick metrics snapshot
- Routing: quota adjustments and edgecase backlog
- Auth: token rotation canary / failure modes seen
- Control plane: scheduler regressions and mitigation plan
- Action items + owners

1) Metrics snapshot (last 72h)
- Avg p95 control-plane RPC latency: 130ms (target 120ms). Notable spike at 2026-10-06 03:14 UTC correlated with quota-eviction events.
- Routing fallthrough rate to fallback-pool: 0.7% (baseline 0.2%).
- Quota exhausts triggered: 11 (customer-facing throttles: 2). Most exhausted buckets were short-burst API keys in region-eu-west.
- Auth error rate: 0.12% token validation failures (up from 0.03%). Mostly expired-token errors during midnight rolling KMS key maintenance.

2) Routing / quotas notes
- Root cause hypothesis for p95 spike: allocator's burst-limiter incorrectly calculated effective capacity during small-node churn; when a node restarted it reported capacity=0 briefly causing backpressure and immediate routing fallthrough -> spike. Marcus to reproduce in staging. Related ticket: PLTFM-869.
- Temporary mitigation applied: increase soft buffer window from 1s -> 3s to tolerate ephemeral node misreports. Deployed as hotfix 2026-10-06 07:12 UTC. Observed partial reduction, but not full.
- Proposal: implement a two-step capacity-report handshake (node reports 'draining' then 'drained') to avoid transient 0-capacity signals. Design backlog: PLTFM-892 (planning).
- Quota tuning: short-term: increase per-key burst-credit for EU region by 15% to reduce customer-facing throttles. Priya to file PR and coordinate billing-related notices.

3) Auth notes
- Token rotation canary (week 1): rolled 10% of traffic through new key rotation flow. Observed an uptick in expired-token errors tied to clients that cache tokens for >TTL.
- Action: augment canary with 'grace header' that returns Retry-After + human-friendly guidance for SDKs. Evan to prototype.
- Backup: fallback to legacy validation path for 5xxs to reduce customer impact. Implemented as short-lived circuit breaker.

4) Control plane scheduler/regression
- Two regressions surfaced in scheduler after recent allocation refactor: (a) rebalancer overshot target counts for micro-pools, (b) checksum mismatch caused extra re-sync churn. Both increase control-plane write QPS and contribute to p95.
- Short-term rollback candidate: revert rebalancer proportional change 8c9f2 -> last good at 7a3d1. Decision deferred until Marcus reproduces locally.
- Long-term: add unit tests for rebalancer targets and add an audit log to rebalancer decisions. Aisha to draft RFC and schedule 1-2 week work.

5) Canary health and observability gaps
- Canary dashboards show CPU tail at +12% during rebalance windows. Missing trace correlation between quota-exhaust events and identity validation calls. We need a lightweight correlation id propagated from frontdoor -> allocator -> auth.
- Proposed quick fix: add ephemeral request id header in frontdoor and log at debug for 24h on canary. Sofia to coordinate with frontdoor team.

6) Incidental items / brain scratchpad
- Idea: prefill KV cache for frequently used prompt prefixes at model-router level during low-load windows. Could cut token-latency for repeated short prompts. (brain: test with synthetic workload hitting same prefix set).
- Question: can we safely relax some quota heuristics for verified enterprise tenants (reduce burst penalties) without re-opening DOS vectors? Needs security review.

7) Action items (owner / ETA / ticket)
- Marcus: reproduce allocator churn locally and create repro harness (ETA: 2026-10-09) -> PLTFM-869.
- Priya: PR for EU burst-credit bump + customer comms draft (ETA: 2026-10-08) -> PLTFM-877.
- Evan: prototype 'grace header' and fallback wiring for token rotation canary (ETA: 2026-10-11) -> PLTFM-884.
- Sofia: add ephemeral request-id propagation in frontdoor for canary (ETA: 2026-10-10) -> PLTFM-893.
- Aisha: draft RFC for rebalancer hardening + test plan (ETA: 2026-10-14) -> PLTFM-892.
- Leila (SRE): run 24h canary with debug logging window and collect correlation traces (ETA: 2026-10-09).

8) Open questions to resolve next sync
- Is the two-step capacity handshake acceptable complexity vs mitigation gains? (engineering + release)
- Do we need a temporary SLA communication for affected customers re: quota sensitivity? (CS + Product)
- What's the threshold for rolling back the allocation refactor if canary metrics don't improve? Define exact metric gates before rollback.

Notes to self / misc fragments:
- "If allocator thinks capacity is 0 for <5s treat as transient" — quick rule but needs careful safety checks.
- Remember to add test coverage for reported 0-capacity state.
- Slack refs: #platform-controlplane thread "eviction-surge-1006" (see pinned messages).

Next short sync: 2026-10-12 10:00 PT (standup will be focused on reproducer progress and canary telemetry).

Log end.
